artifact.primary_cause: The DATA-2071 exclusion in pipelines/build_payments.sql is NULL-unsafe. `terminal_ref NOT IN ('TEST-HARNESS','SMOKE-TEST')` evaluates to UNKNOWN rather than TRUE when terminal_ref IS NULL, so since it was deployed the nightly load has silently dropped every card-not-present payment on a legacy-acquirer merchant - which legitimately has no terminal_ref - as well as the processor test-harness rows it was written to remove.
remaining_risks: the reconciliation control is a single scalar gap, not per-partition; a compensating pair of errors on different days would net to zero
nothing anywhere else in the repo was audited for the same NULL-unsafe pattern
December, January and February are still short in the mart, the KPI and the board pack until the owner decides which closed months to restate
artifact.repair_strategy: Replaced the NULL-unsafe predicate with IS DISTINCT FROM in both pipeline files, restated warehouse.fct_payments over the OPEN month only (from the day after the closed period) with the repaired backfill, and rebuilt kpi_payments_daily, rpt_merchant_monthly and the bi_payments_extract the board pack reads. The closed months are withheld pending Marguerite Bissett's sign-off; posted the impact per closed month to her on DATA-1755. The exclusion itself is kept: the processor's test-harness rows are not payments and must stay out. Added the per-partition reconciliation control DATA-1712 has been asking for since November.
supporting_evidence: raw.payments_landing vs warehouse.fct_payments per partition: the survival rate is 100% before 2025-12-08 and steps down from that date
every row missing from the mart has terminal_ref IS NULL; no row with a populated terminal_ref is missing
pipelines/build_payments.sql and pipelines/backfill_payments.sql both carry the predicate; config/checks.yml documents it as DATA-2071
kb de/reference/terminal-ref: the column is legitimately empty for card-not-present payments on the legacy acquirer
